subject: General Knowledge
topic: Animals, wildlife & national symbols — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The Indian Elephant was officially designated as India's National Heritage Animal in which year?

options.option_text: 2006 (during the Eleventh Five Year Plan period)
2010 (declared by MoEFCC under Project Elephant)
2008 (the year of National Tiger Conservation setup)
2014 (year of a major Wildlife Protection Act review)

questions.explanation: The Indian Elephant was declared India's National Heritage Animal in October 2010 by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, recognising its deep cultural and ecological significance. Option A (2006) is wrong — it predates the declaration; some candidates confuse it with unrelated wildlife policy milestones. Option C (2008) is a distractor linked to NTCA's formal operationalisation period.

questions.stem: The Chinkara (Indian Gazelle) is the official state animal of which Indian state?

options.option_text: Gujarat, which is also home to the Asiatic Lion
Haryana, bordering the national capital Delhi
Rajasthan, the largest state by area in India
Madhya Pradesh, widely known as the Tiger State

questions.explanation: Chinkara (Gazella bennettii) is the state animal of Rajasthan, well adapted to the Thar Desert's arid terrain. Gujarat (option A) is the most tempting distractor because it shares desert habitat with Chinkara, but Gujarat's state animal is the Asiatic Lion. Madhya Pradesh's state animal is the Swamp Deer (Barasingha).

questions.stem: Project Elephant, India's centrally sponsored scheme for in-situ elephant conservation, was launched in which year?

options.option_text: 1973 (the same year Project Tiger was launched)
1986 (when India's first Biosphere Reserve was formed)
1992 (during the Eighth Five-Year Plan period)
2001 (following the National Wildlife Action Plan meet)

questions.explanation: Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 by the Government of India under the 8th Five-Year Plan to protect elephants, their habitats and corridors. Option A (1973) is the classic distractor — that is when Project Tiger was launched, and many candidates conflate the two flagship programmes.

questions.stem: As per the 2022 All-India Tiger Estimation, which tiger reserve recorded the highest individual tiger count in the country?

options.option_text: Ranthambore Tiger Reserve located in Rajasthan
Bandipur Tiger Reserve located in Karnataka
Jim Corbett National Park located in Uttarakhand
Nagarhole Tiger Reserve located in Karnataka

questions.explanation: The 2022 census reported a national total of 3,167 tigers; Jim Corbett NP had the highest single-reserve count at approximately 260. Options B and D (Bandipur and Nagarhole) together form the biodiverse Nilgiri landscape and are common distractors because Karnataka has the highest state-level tiger count, but individually neither reserve surpasses Corbett.

questions.stem: India's first Biosphere Reserve, the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, was established under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere Programme in which year?

options.option_text: 1973 (same year Project Tiger was formally launched)
1980 (the year the Forest Conservation Act was passed)
1986 (spanning Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka)
1991 (the year before the Rio Earth Summit in Brazil)

questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was designated in 1986 as India's first under the UNESCO MAB Programme, covering the Western Ghats tri-junction. Option A (1973) is a common error — that year is strongly associated with Project Tiger. Option D (1991) is a plausible distractor since many candidates anchor biosphere activity to the Rio Summit era.

questions.stem: The Snow Leopard (Panthera uncia) was reclassified in 2017 on the IUCN Red List — from 'Endangered' to which new status?

options.option_text: Near Threatened — population decline found to have slowed
Vulnerable — still faces high extinction risk in the wild
Least Concern — global population now considered stable
Critically Endangered — revised downward on newer survey data

questions.explanation: In 2017, IUCN downlisted the Snow Leopard from Endangered to Vulnerable based on revised global population estimates of 4,000–6,500 individuals; the species still qualifies as threatened. Option A (Near Threatened) is wrong — NT means the species barely misses threatened criteria, which is not the case here. Option D is factually inverted — the status was relaxed, not tightened.

questions.stem: Keibul Lamjao National Park, the world's only floating national park, is the sole natural habitat of which critically endangered deer?

options.option_text: Barasingha (Swamp Deer), emblematic of Kanha Reserve
Hangul (Kashmir Stag), protected in Dachigam Reserve
Sangai (Brow-antlered Deer), endemic to Manipur state
Musk Deer, inhabiting high-altitude Himalayan alpine zones

questions.explanation: Keibul Lamjao NP floats on the phumdis (floating biomass) of Loktak Lake in Manipur and is the last natural refuge of the Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii), also called the dancing deer. Option B (Hangul) is the most tempting distractor as it is another critically endangered, range-restricted Indian deer, but it lives in Dachigam NP, Jammu & Kashmir — a distinct habitat entirely.
